definition.note: The attempted k >= 3 dihedral symmetrization of Wohlgemuth's genus-3 handle surface.  Its failure questions the folklore that a surface existing for some dihedral order k exists for all larger k.

construction.blocked_by: BELIEVED NOT TO EXIST on numerical evidence -- a weaker statement than a proof, and a stronger one than 'unbuilt'.  Weber reports that raising the dihedral symmetry of Wohlgemuth's second surface (genus 3) to k = 3 fails: at k = 2.999 the numerically solved periods do not appear to close, and for larger k the period problem could not be solved at all.  Weber files it under Non-Existent Surfaces.
construction.resume: A proof either way would settle it; the mirrored page poses the underlying free-boundary deformation question explicitly.  The existing k = 2 surface has its own record (wohlgemuth-second-surface-genus-3).

provenance.definition: Not transcribed. The record exists to state that the surface is absent and why; a fabricated equation would be worse than a null.
sources: M. Weber, 'Wohlgemuth's Second Surface (which documents the failed dihedralization)', minimalsurfaces.blog (local mirror: minsurf/book/.../ch418_wohlgemuths_second_surface.md).
M. Weber, 'Non-Existent Surfaces (section index)', minimalsurfaces.blog (local mirror: minsurf/book/.../ch061_non_existent_surfaces.md).
M. Wohlgemuth, 'Minimal surfaces of higher genus with finite total curvature', Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 137 (1997) 1-25 (the existing k = 2 surface).
